subQuests.subQuestName: Return to your room to rest

60100101.text: Ergh, so much noise... What's going on this time...

60100102.text: Hey! Where's Flins!? Is he here, or isn't he?

60100103.text: We would be most obliged if you would pipe down a little, dear guest. Our other guests are resting...

60100104.text: Resting!? We're all about to be done for, and you're talking about rest!?

60100105.text: Flins is a Wild Hunt shapeshifter, here to deceive us all! If we don't get rid of him now, there'll be no end to this!

60100106.text: You'd better give him up — if anything happens, your business here is done for. You want that, huh?

60100107.text: Or are you in cahoots with him? You with the Wild Hunt too, huh?

60100108.text: What happened? Did something leak out?

60100109.text: But we were so careful last night... How did anyone see us?

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the "Curatorium of Secrets" to inform your companions of the new intel

60100201.text: I see. So Flins has a fragment taken from within a Wild Hunt anomaly...

60100202.text: Is he gonna be okay now that he's on his own again?

60100203.text: Earlier, he said that the fragment had gone still, so it's probably of no use to Rerir now.

60100204.text: In that case, Rerir shouldn't have any reason to keep pursuing him, right? So was all that ruckus back at The Flagship just an act of spite, or what?

60100205.text: If I were him, I would have simply turned my attention to collecting other fragments.

60100206.text: #A reasonable course of action. Remember what we heard back at the tavern, {NICKNAME}? The actual number of Wild Hunt anomalies destroyed has been greater than Lightkeeper records would indicate.

60100207.text: Some of these must have been Rerir's doing. He must have been seeking more fragments.

60100208.text: This much is pretty easy to understand... But why would he pretend to be Sousi and put so much effort into getting the cannon up and running again?

60100209.text: Maybe 'cause that'd be more efficient than having to clear anomalies himself?

60100212.text: Yeah, I'm confident that the ammo we're packing has the oomph to do that. But I am a mechanic, after all — for me, test data and their conclusions speak loudest.

60100213.text: Why don't we find a few of those fragments ourselves and use kuuvahki to carry out a little experiment?

60100214.text: Our lab could certainly accommodate such a test.

60100215.text: In other words, we gotta destroy a couple of anomalies and collect fragments from them, right?

60100216.text: Lightkeeper operations have just about ceased following the Sergeant Major's passing.

60100217.text: Meanwhile, the Wild Hunt continues to grow in scale by the day... I fear only we can keep the situation under control now.

60100218.text: Then we'd best act fast. Paimon's got a bad feeling about this...

60100219.text: A feeling we all share, I'm afraid.

60100220.text: (The fragments, the cannon, kuuvahki, Rerir, and the Abyss... There must be some thread linking all these factors together.)

60100221.text: (Besides, is getting revenge on Flins truly Rerir's sole aim?)

60100222.text: (We're missing some decisive connection here, but we're running out of time.)

60100223.text: There are three Wild Hunt sites that must be dealt with urgently... But I believe we have the capacity to handle it.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the Final Night Cemetery to meet Flins

60100301.text: No one's guarding this place, just like he said. But, uh, where do we find the information he mentioned?

60100303.text: Let's move. We're running out of time.

60100304.text: Ah, there you are! Okay, let's split up and make this happen...

60100305.text: ...Or not! How are we supposed to read through this many files!?

60100307.text: Difficult, yes, but it is also our most efficient option.

60100308.text: To expose the true intentions of this Rerir, we need to dive into Nod-Krai's history.

60100309.text: *sigh* Hope we don't land on our heads, then...

60100312.text: That file s—s—suddenly moved by itself!

60100313.text: This is a graveyard, right, Flins? D—Do these things just kinda... happen?

60100314.text: Many strange things happen here, but this is not one of them.

60100315.text: B—But that file really did m—m—move by itself!

60100316.text: Hey, come out! D—Don't scare Paimon like that!

60100322.text: Are we... being given hints? I feel no hostility. On the contrary — it seems we're being aided, somehow.

60100323.text: Really? H—Hey, seriously, another one? O—Okay, then... Paimon'll read this one!

60100324.text: Phew, finally finished! Paimon sure could use a long break from long words now... Hope she can remember it all.

60100325.text: The material I've read through has all been about past Wild Hunt incidents of enormous scale. What about you?

60100327.text: Paimon as well! Guess that makes three of us.

60100328.text: Hmm. Whatever this is, it seems to want us to notice something. Let's bring our files together and give them another look through.

60100330.text: Hmm, all these incidents look pretty different...

60100331.text: Wait, I've noticed something. Before the occurrence of these huge Wild Hunt events, a smaller-scale one would erupt in the exact same location.

60100332.text: And look — all these smaller-scale Wild Hunt site reports share a common outcome.

60100333.text: They'd be detected, but would go inactive before any forces could be sent to deal with them. They could then be sealed directly using a Tideseal Stone... Eh, but why?

60100334.text: Was Rerir actively clearing these sites?

60100335.text: Some of these records are too old. I doubt he had regained the ability to act freely yet, or we would have met long ago.

60100336.text: Ah, and here's another similarity! "Kuuvahki in nearby soil completely drained." Could this be important, somehow?

60100337.text: Kuuvahki and the Wild Hunt are mutually opposed forces.

60100338.text: We Lightkeepers previously believed that these small Wild Hunt sites would temporarily go inactive due to being neutralized by the kuuvahki present in the soil.

60100339.text: But now that we've synthesized all this data, there is a key issue this hypothesis cannot explain...

60100342.text: Indeed. Despite the name, I would not call a Tideseal Stone's sealing powers "watertight," exactly — but for it to fail and the situation to deteriorate in such short order...

60100343.text: Urgh... Paimon feels like she's almost got it...

60100344.text: (The Wild Hunt was not suppressed by kuuvahki. Instead, it became stronger...)

60100345.text: (And Rerir wants to use Aino's cannon, the ammo of which is also made using kuuvahki...)

60100348.text: Yes, that might be it. It could be that when kuuvahki and Abyssal energies meet, the stronger side will suppress the weaker one.

60100349.text: And while kuuvahki can indeed destroy small-scale Wild Hunt anomalies, should Rerir be strong enough... the kuuvahki might be his for the taking instead.

60100350.text: P—Paimon kinda gets where we're going with this!

subQuests.subQuestName: Rush to Starsand Shoal to stop Rerir

60100402.text: Humans... You never change. Always trying to use powers you neither comprehend nor control.

60100403.text: But it is also thanks to you that I found a way to return.

60100404.text: You've messed with the cannon again, huh? Sorry, but this round's not gonna go your way!

60100405.text: Ah, hahaha... Such faith in your companions.

60100406.text: But will the inhabitants of Nasha Town understand why they wish to stop the cannon? I think not.

60100407.text: When all they see is the Wild Hunt surging up everywhere they look, the cannon must seem like their only lifeline.

60100408.text: This is the truth I have revealed to them.

60100411.text: They did this all of their own volition.

60100412.text: The zealous worship of power leads only to annihilation of equally zealous proportions. True power does not heed the commands of the weak.

60100413.text: You were waiting for us to leave Nasha Town, then.

60100414.text: Of course. I imagine the one you call "Aino" would have managed to stop the cannon otherwise. Shame, then, that you proved one step too slow.

60100415.text: In their folly, the townspeople will bar the path of all who seek to stop the cannon — and your kind-hearted, weak companions have not the stomach to deal with them. The cannon will not be stopped now.

60100416.text: Well, sir, you look most pleased with yourself. In that case, before you put us out of our misery, I would like to ask you a question, if I may.

60100417.text: See this fragment? It once haunted your dreams, but now, it seems useless to you. What is it, exactly?

60100420.text: My body was once torn into countless pieces and hurled into the swirling chaos of time itself. But even so, my life and will were not extinguished.

60100421.text: Ah... Every last fragment calls to me. Sooner or later, they shall welcome my return.

60100423.text: Huh, so the terror of the Wild Hunt was, in fact, caused by scattered pieces of your corpse... I guess they don't call you one of the Five Sinners for nothing.

60100424.text: Hmph. Serendipity guided the fragments to construct an incomplete version of myself, upon which I began collecting more within Wild Hunt sites across the land...

60100425.text: But each time, the fragments I obtained were hardly worth mentioning.

60100426.text: While that which you hold in your hand... was my heart.

60100427.text: So that's why it responded so strongly to you.

60100428.text: Only by retrieving this most critical piece could I gain mastery over the turbulent kuuvahki energies and be fully reborn.

60100429.text: Hence you fired that first shot hoping to regain enough power to seize the fragment from me.

60100430.text: Are you completely crazy? Weren't you afraid of dying?

60100431.text: Dying? Hahaha... Such power has no hope of killing me. It may destroy my form over and over, yet always, I rebuild it. It may smash my flesh and crush my bones, thousands of times and more, but that is of no consequence to me.

60100432.text: What truly infuriates me, however, is how you've destroyed my heart. All that suffering, everything I endured... and all for nothing!

subQuests.subQuestName: Enter Nasha Town, now in chaos
Talk to everyone in front of town

60100501.text: Dang it, who fired up the cannon without my say-so!?

60100502.text: Its defensive barrier has also been activated, likely in anticipation of interference by malicious actors.

60100503.text: The air is thick with fear and anxiety... It's spooking the birds and beasts. What exactly is going on?

60100504.text: You're here. Looks like this was all part of Rerir's plan. Not only did he plant seeds of suspicion in people's hearts... Seems he's now igniting them.

60100505.text: Jahoda's gone in to scout out the situation. She'll be back any minute—

60100506.text: I'm back, I'm back! Oh, it's bad out there. Rumors flying everywhere you turn... Something about the Wild Hunt preparing to spawn a wave of monsters, the likes of which we've never seen before...

60100507.text: ...But that's not even the worst of it.

60100508.text: Lots of folks don't even believe the cannon can prevent this crisis, so they're getting ready to make a run for it. Others are trying to make a quick buck out of this whole mess...

60100509.text: How could they still be thinking about Mora when such a catastrophe is imminent...?

60100510.text: Unprecedented danger brings unprecedented opportunities in its wake... A chaotic situation can bury much wrongdoing.

60100511.text: Even those who flee without reserve put themselves at the mercy of the divine. Is it any wonder, then, that some will aim to profit?

60100512.text: After all, a gamble that might rewrite one's entire life is hard to come by.

60100514.text: Well, seeing as you disapprove of their actions so strongly, Lady Moonchanter, I suggest that you be the one to handle them. Not like that's the only major problem on our plate right now...

60100515.text: Affirmative. We must quell the chaos in Nasha Town as soon as possible. Also, the unexpected activation of the cannon entails a high risk of incorrect operation. This must be stopped in a timely manner.

60100516.text: Well, about that... People have been talking about how someone might come to stop the cannon. They've decided they won't let anyone in.

60100517.text: What!? I made that thing! They can't just take it from me! Let me over there — what are they gonna do, stop me?

60100518.text: They might, if Rerir has already formulated some countermeasure.

60100519.text: For example, he might have spread a rumor that the Wild Hunt would take your form...

60100521.text: Possibility: High. If they view the cannon as Nasha Town's only hope, they are likely to conclude that anyone who tries to stop it must be with the Wild Hunt.

60100522.text: We will face strong resistance, but they are just ordinary people. Brute force must be avoided if possible.

60100523.text: There's no time. Let's go into the town. I'll find some way to calm the townspeople, you find a way to stop the cannon.

60100524.text: Oh, you're back. Mm? And you have a letter?

60100525.text: #...{NICKNAME} won't make it back in time, so they're heading straight over to Starsand Shoal instead.

60100526.text: #Wait, what? Isn't that the cannon's target? Why would {M#he}{F#she} go there!?

60100528.text: So if we can't prevent the cannon from being fired...

60100530.text: #And we must ensure that {M#his}{F#her} trust in us is not misplaced. Let's go.

60100701.text: Most of those we've met so far have been attempting to escape, so they haven't gotten in our way. But it won't be so easy from here on out.

60100702.text: Looks like they've formed groups to protect the cannon. If they believe that we're with the Wild Hunt, we'll have no choice but to force our way through.

60100703.text: Is that... Lady Lauma? But... are you... really her?

60100704.text: Ah, it's you, Ryksa. I believe you recognize this power, having lived on Hiisi Island for so long. It is not something that anyone else could imitate.

60100705.text: I do, yes... So it really is you, my Lady.

60100706.text: But why are you here? Really, I... I believe you, but the others... Well, they'll be on high alert.

60100707.text: The townspeople have been misled into believing that they needed to activate the cannon. I am here to stop them.

60100709.text: I know what you wish to say. Our island and Nasha Town have never had close ties. There should be no reason for me to intervene.

60100710.text: But you chose to leave the island — you had the resolve and the courage to start a new life.

60100711.text: It is unfair — unjust — that you should be dragged into this mess just as that life was about to begin.

60100712.text: I seek to redress this injustice, not only for you, but for everyone here who wishes to live their lives free from this chaos.

60100713.text: Please, have faith in our longstanding friendship... and that this is where my heart has led me.

60100714.text: ...Thank you, my Lady, thank you... Please, help us.

60100715.text: Then come. I need you to step forward alongside me, and to do your part too.

60100717.text: Hah, seems we chose the right person for the job. Alright, everyone — let us meet again later.

60100718.text: Huh? You're not coming with us?

60100719.text: We won't be able to calm this storm by our power alone. As such, I'll need to contact some... Let's call them friends in high places, shall we?

60100721.text: O—Okay...! See you again, everyone... Um, that is, if we can...

60102101.text: Lady Moonchanter, there's a child here!

60100801.text: Thank you for bringing us here. We can quickly overcome the barrier by going upward from over there.

60100802.text: The cannon is all yours now.

60100803.text: Got it. Thanks, Lauma. Ineffa, give her a krumkake.

60100804.text: Orders received and immediately deferred. Departure takes priority—

60100806.text: I will not deny that we hold different beliefs, but in the face of the immense threat that hangs above us all, we must persist in trusting one another.

60100807.text: Otherwise, rifts will surely form, prized open by those who harbor ulterior motives.

60100808.text: If your fear is born of helplessness, if you flee because you know not how to fight, then follow me, you who are lost.

60100809.text: I am no god, but so long as we hold our candles steady and unite beneath the same moonlight, no deception or rumors can be concealed from us.

60100810.text: Let us resolve, then, to defend ourselves — and to stand firm against the false illusions by which our foe seeks to beguile us!

subQuests.subQuestName: Try to get close to the cannon

60101101.text: This isn't good, Ineffa. We gotta hurry!

60101102.text: Scanning... Kuuvahki ammunition fully loaded. Preheating complete. The cannon is going through its final pre-fire checks.

60101103.text: *sigh* ... Alright. Let's hit the emergency brake.

60101104.text: Assessment: Not enough time. Emergency brake will cause internal explosion of stored kuuvahki. Damage assessment: Incalculable. Nasha Town likely to be blasted skyward.

60101105.text: No, no! I mean a manual brake. You know, the primitive kind.

60101202.text: Sluggish, torpid... This body is a disappointment.

60101203.text: I can barely muster... Tsk, ten percent of my original strength... You've ruined everything, again...

60101204.text: Let me guess... You didn't get a human body back, did you?

60101207.text: (This is bad! His presence feels completely different now... He's even stronger than before!)

60101209.text: Watch out! Whatever rationality he still had when he was searching for his body is gone... All that's left is the calamity you see before you, a monster fueled by nothing but his own obsession!

60101210.text: It matters not... Having a heart... Being human... It's all irrelevant, completely and utterly insignificant!

60101211.text: You! You matter not... Nor does anything in this world! Gah! Argh, argh! None of it matters to me!

60101403.text: It seems my time... is running out...

60100601.text: It's getting late. The situation is urgent, but rest is vital. Good night, both of you.

60101302.text: It seems this young lady aided in our escape. You have my sincere gratitude, dear madame.

60101303.text: The flowers here bloom in such peaceful silence. I imagine you would not have invited anyone here, were it not an emergency.

60101304.text: Huh, talk about a good judge of character...

60101305.text: Oh? I take it that means you've been here before, then? In that case, I count myself fortunate to be your associate.

60101306.text: Columbinaaaa... What did you do that for!?!?

60101307.text: I studied his abilities inside-out... Equipped Pulonia with comprehensive countermeasures... We were going to settle the score...!

60101308.text: But he still broke through, did he not?

60101309.text: What, you expect a battle to be completely one-sided!?

60101310.text: I just... didn't expect him to have no sense of honor, whatsoever! Pulonia would have been fine in a head-on clash, but battles just... get chaotic...

60101311.text: Oh... So you actually thought you could win.

60101312.text: Have you been taking care of yourself lately? Your calculations seem to have deviated quite seriously. Perhaps you could try sleeping and rising earlier, or you could adopt my previous recommendation and—

60101313.text: Hey, listen here, Columbina! I tolerated your nonsense previously because we were colleagues.

60101314.text: There's a Fatui warrant out on your head, and don't you forget that. Don't make me fight you right here and now.

60101315.text: Oh, I was just a little concerned about you, that's all... Just like that time when you weren't making any progress with your research, so you went and cooped yourself up all alone...

60101316.text: That was none of your business! And don't you ever drag me out to one of your freaky hovels again!

60101321.text: I was worried about you, too — not only because the remains of the Eternal Moon Goddess cannot fall into his hands, but also... because you've done much for me yourselves.

60101322.text: And then I... Well, I brought your associate along for the ride, too. But that was as much as I could do.

60101323.text: You're not afraid to speak your mind, miss — I like that. Please, call me Flins. It is my honor to make the acquaintance of one such as yourself.

60101324.text: Still, what do we do now? Rerir's gotten stronger again. At this point, it doesn't seem like we can beat him.

60101325.text: We did block most of the kuuvahki, so I'd say we've put a lid on his plans, for now at least.

60101326.text: But we still don't know what his aims are, and he may continue gathering power... So we must be very careful.

60101327.text: After you left, I could no longer sense his presence...

60101328.text: That means it's safe out there for now, right?

60101329.text: A question, if I may, kind Miss Columbina.

60101330.text: When the cannon's kuuvahki beam was deflected earlier, I saw several bolts of energy streak toward Hiisi Island, only to be blocked. Did you also have a hand in that?

60101333.text: Oh, yeah. The cannon veered off course in the end, didn't it? Paimon wonders how Aino and the others are doing. Let's head back and check on them!

60101334.text: In that case, Miss Columbina, I shall not disturb your serenity any longer. Thank you once again for coming to the rescue.

60101335.text: Go now, all of you. Do not worry.

60109903.text: Remember these words: "The road shall be paved with truth, and we shall pave it ourselves."

60109904.text: It's... It's you, Lady Moonchanter! It's her, everyone. It's her!

60109905.text: You're right, my Lady. At times like these, we must rely on ourselves!

60109911.text: Leave this to us, Lady Moonchanter! Go!

60109912.text: I always knew something was off about you. You're actually some Abyssal creature, aren't you?

60109913.text: Time to teach you a lesson you won't forget!

60109914.text: Please, calm down. They're clearly innocent!

60109922.text: What are you waiting for!? Let's get outta here!

60109923.text: I'm never coming back to this lousy place again!

60109925.text: You wretched monsters! You're not getting anywhere near the cannon!

60109926.text: The monsters you fear do not exist here. The madness you have fallen to has been the source of untold disasters.

60109927.text: You think we had a choice!?

60109928.text: "Destiny" is no excuse for greed and destruction.

60109929.text: The choice has always been yours to make, and it remains so even now.
